_doc: Host profile for BeTenshi. THE DEFAULT: any machine the console cannot identify (a Vercel build box, a fresh clone) resolves to this profile, so a deployed console keeps targeting BeTenshi's public hostnames exactly as it always has. Selected by hostname 'BeTenshi' or HOST_ID=betenshi. See src/lib/host.ts.
name: BeTenshi

memory._doc: A 32 GB card and a 63 GB host are SEPARATE budgets. Everything in ram-budget.ts, the reserved/peak footprint split and the refuse-if-it-will-not-fit guard exists because of this. Do not copy that reasoning to a unified-memory host.

services.name: Service Manager
services.note: The supervisor every other Start/Stop button goes through — when this is down the console reports 'Manager error: fetch failed' on every service and nothing can be started, so it needs to be visible rather than invisible infrastructure. Owned by the 'BeTenshi Manager' scheduled task: fires at logon and auto-restarts within a minute if the process dies, which also makes a stray Stop on this card self-healing.

services.name: Chatterbox Voice
services.note: Second TTS engine, kept BELOW Kokoro deliberately: defaultServiceFor() takes the first service that serves a capability, so a router outage still falls back to the 82M model that answers in 300ms rather than the 0.5B one that clones. Reachable at /v1/audio/voices for enrolling a reference clip.

services.name: ACE-Step Music
services.note: ACE-Step 1.5: an XL (4B, int8) diffusion renderer planned by a 1.7B 5Hz LM, both offloaded between phases so it fits beside quote-forge's resident vllm-small (+5 GB idle, +9 GB peak, measured). Text + optional lyrics -> a full song; also repaint/extend and restyle an uploaded clip, and (on the base DiT) extract stems. /health is 503 until the ~30 s model load finishes; /status says which phase it is in. What it can do is asked of the engine at /v1/music/capabilities, not declared here.

services.name: Qwen-Image
services.note: Local 20B Qwen-Image diffusion model (RTX 5090, fp8). Text→image today; image-edit (Qwen-Image-Edit) is wired in the console but gated server-side. server: hq/quote-forge/server/qwen_image.py — POST /generate, POST /edit, GET /health

services.name: ComfyUI
services.note: Categorised as an APP, not an AI backend: it's a browser workflow UI you open and drive by hand (its card CTA is 'Open ↗', like Open WebUI), rather than a headless model server other code calls. It does use the GPU, but that's shown per-card as VRAM instead of being a category.

services.name: SAM 3D Body
services.note: Meta SAM 3D Body — single-image full-body 3D human mesh + pose recovery. Resident FastAPI service (move-quest: services/sam3d/server.py). POST /pose {image, bbox?} -> 70-joint 3D skeleton + global rotation (+ optional body mesh); correct on floor/inverted/acro poses.

services.name: SAM 3
services.note: Meta SAM 3 — open-vocabulary promptable concept segmentation. Give it an image + a text concept ('person', 'car') and it segments every matching instance (masks + boxes + scores). Resident FastAPI service (move-quest: services/sam3/server.py). POST /segment {image, concepts}.

services.name: TRELLIS.2 (trellis.cpp)
services.note: Image -> textured 3D mesh (GLB, PBR, UV atlas). Microsoft TRELLIS.2-4B, and TencentARC's Pixal3D fine-tune of it, on trellis.cpp: a C++/GGML port with prebuilt Windows CUDA binaries, chosen because the reference PyTorch pipeline needs CUDA extensions (o-voxel, cumesh, flex_gemm, nvdiffrast) this box has no toolkit or MSVC to build. The server is resident but loads and frees each stage per request, so between meshes it keeps only its CUDA context and ggml pool (1.3 GB measured). POST /generate multipart {image, seed, resolution 512|1024|1536, model trellis|pixal3d}. localOnly: a bare HTTP API with no auth.

services.name: TripoSR
services.note: Fast feed-forward image -> mesh (Stability AI + Tripo, MIT). The 'blockout in a second' half of the 3D Lab: vertex-coloured, no UV texture. FastAPI wrapper in C:\Users\Admin\Code\AI\triposr (own venv; torchmcubes swapped for PyMCubes because it needs a CUDA build). POST /generate multipart {image, resolution (marching-cubes grid), bg_removal}; replies with timing and torch-peak headers.

services.name: Process engine (Operaton)
services.note: Operaton 2.1.4 (Apache-2.0 fork of Camunda 7): executes the process lab's BPMN 2.0 processes and DMN 1.3 decisions, with Cockpit and Tasklist at /operaton/app/. Docker container 'process-engine' from C:\Users\Admin\Code\AI\process-lab\docker-compose.yml; H2 in a named volume. No GPU; measured 628 MiB RAM with 16 cases in flight (docker stats, 27 Sep 2026). localOnly and bound to 127.0.0.1: the REST API is unauthenticated. Why this engine: process-lab/docs/engine-choice.md.

services.name: SearXNG (web search)
services.note: Self-hosted metasearch (Brave, Google, Bing, Wikipedia and more) so a local model can search the web for free: the Video Forge's search tool calls /search?format=json. Docker container 'searxng' (searxng/searxng), published on 127.0.0.1:8888 only, restart unless-stopped; settings in C:\Users\Admin\Code\AI\searxng\settings.yml, secret in the container env. No GPU; ~125 MB RAM measured (docker stats, 30 Sep 2026). DuckDuckGo answers it with a CAPTCHA; the other engines work. localOnly: it must never be exposed.

services.name: Process lab
services.note: A simulated relocation agency: external-task workers (Laya via /api/decide, Gemma 4 via the AI Router, local first with a recorded cloud fallback), the simulator, and the JSON API the Process Lab tab reads. Node 24, no dependencies; C:\Users\Admin\Code\AI\process-lab. Needs process-engine. Holds no GPU memory itself (measured ~110 MB RAM); its Ollama calls take the coordinator's ollama-chat lease and honour logs/gpu-claim.txt.

services.name: Laya decisions
services.note: Convai Innovations' Laya (Apache-2.0): typed decisions (pick a choice, yes/no, score) with a probability per option from one forward pass. Not a text generator. Runs on CPU on purpose (~150-300 ms a decision, ~4-5 GB RAM, no VRAM): on the 5090 it is ~30 ms but holds ~6 GB of a contended card. 'laya' routes each request to the English or multilingual checkpoint by script; typed-decisions loads on first use. Zero-shot it is well short of an LLM on this box's own decisions; see docs/decision-model-experiment-2026-09-27.md before relying on it. POST /decide; the console contract is POST /api/decide (docs/decide-api.md). localOnly: no auth, bound to 127.0.0.1 like the AI Router.

services.name: Ollama (Gemma 4 / Qwen3-VL)
services.note: The box's SECOND LLM runtime, beside vLLM, and not redundancy. vLLM pins one model and reserves its VRAM at startup - the right shape for something called all day. Ollama loads a model on demand and evicts it after OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE - the right shape for evaluation and for capabilities used occasionally, like vision. It exists at all because vLLM cannot serve Gemma 4: the image on this box is 0.17.1 and has no gemma4 architecture (needs >= 0.19, a ~30 GB pull), verified against the running container rather than assumed. localOnly for the same reason as the router: a bare HTTP API with no auth, which must never acquire a tunnel hostname. Usually started by the Ollama tray app, which is fine - externalPid() adopts the running process and Stop still works.

services.name: AI Router
services.note: AI Router — a LiteLLM proxy giving one OpenAI-compatible endpoint for every model this box can reach: local (vLLM, Qwen-Image) and cloud (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic). Model aliases live in config/ai-router.yaml, which is the ONLY place vendor model ids are written. POST /v1/chat/completions — text; POST /v1/images/generations — images. localOnly: bound to 127.0.0.1 with no tunnel hostname (publicUrl is intentionally not a public hostname). It serves systems that use this box's local resources (console, quote-forge, move-quest). Cloud projects must NOT route through it.

workstreams._doc: What this machine can be asked to DO, as the Home page offers it. Lifted verbatim from the hardcoded workflowConfig in home-cockpit.tsx so the page stops advertising work a host cannot do. Keys are fixed (text/image/audio/files); the icon for each is chosen in code. vramGb/ramGb are the measured footprints from model-meta.json, duplicated here only for the pre-flight 'can it run?' panel.
